note: A roomId filter. The request carries no filter: a filter would turn this into "is my principal in THAT room", which is a different question with a different answer and no authorization story of its own. `includePersonal` changes what an entry carries, never which entries come back.
A member filter. The recipient answers for the members its caller may act as; naming one would be a way to ask whether the recipient serves a member the caller does not act as.
Paging members. Rooms are bounded by how many a person is in, so there is no cursor to issue and none to accept.
includePersonal as a string. It is a boolean; a string "false" would read as true in too many languages.
Bare/unnamespaced ext key — SPEC §4.5.1 requires every immediate child of ext to be reverse-DNS namespaced.
An entry with no member. 0.2 names whose group state each entry is, so a room held as two personas is two distinguishable entries and a client can name the one it means.
An empty personal label. A member with no label has no `personal`; an object carrying only `updatedAt` would be a second way to say so.
A personal label with no `updatedAt`. Every label says when it last changed, so a client showing it on several devices can tell which copy is current.
